thread:
maria: Heads-up — Acme escalated. They've got a weird regression: p95/p99 for streaming endpoints up ~600ms. TTFB for streaming is actually better than non-streaming on their path, but total time/p99 is higher and there's a long tail with many small chunks then a big pause. Customer provided a short repro and traces. Request id=req-ACME-20260310-01. Repro below.

ben: Can you paste the exact curl + timings and whether they're using h2 or SSE? region/tenant? Also any SDK version?

maria: curl they used (http2, node client via our SDK with default chunking):
```
curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -d '{"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream 
# measured with time: TTFB=80ms total=850ms
```
Non-streaming same prompt:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -d '{"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
# measured: TTFB=300ms total=420ms
```
So streaming TTFB is much lower but total is worse. They reported chunk pattern: many small early chunks then 600ms silence then last chunk.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled edge-proxy v3.12 -> canary at 3949998000 :rocket:

ravi: What transport are they on? If they're multiplexing many streams on a single h2 connection, head-of-line or flow-control could create that tail. Also check client read loop — backpressure can make us buffer. Any keepalive reuse?

ben: Also check reverse-proxy buffering (nginx/h2 settings) and our chunk-flush heuristic. Enable debug with env: REDWOOD_STREAM_DEBUG=1 and grab logs around req-ACME-20260310-01. Example grep: `rg "req-ACME-20260310-01" /var/log/edge/*.log`

maria: Pasted relevant edge logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-10T12:01:05Z] req-ACME-20260310-01 enter edge
[2026-03-10T12:01:05Z] proxy flush chunk 1 -> t=80ms
[2026-03-10T12:01:05Z] proxy flush chunk 2 -> t=120ms
[2026-03-10T12:01:05Z] runtime emit token batch -> t=140ms
[2026-03-10T12:01:05Z] runtime stall (model) -> t=380ms
[2026-03-10T12:01:05Z] proxy flush chunk N -> t=760ms
[2026-03-10T12:01:06Z] req-ACME-20260310-01 complete -> total=850ms
```
Looks like a model stall at ~380ms then nothing until ~760ms, but customer claims they see packets arriving to client earlier and then final huge gap.

ben: Two hypotheses: (1) model/serving runtime produced tokens slowly (token gen stall); (2) network/coalescing at proxy or client read side delaying final chunk. Quick mitigations: switch tenant to non-streaming fallback (guarantees single response when done) OR enable more aggressive chunk coalescing / reduce max_chunk_wait_ms to 50ms for tenant.

ravi: For triage capture a short pcap on the customer path from edge to client if possible or ask customer to run `tcpdump -i any host api.redwood.ai and port 443 -w /tmp/acme.pcap` during their repro — look for delayed ACKs/Nagle. Also inspect HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE frames; if client window is 0 we will stall.

ben: Config we can apply to tenant quickly (example):
```json
{"tenant":"acme","streaming":{
  "coalesce_window_ms":50,
  "max_emit_batch_tokens":64,
  "fallback_non_streaming":false
}}
```
Apply via admin CLI: `redwood-admin tenants patch acme --json @patch.json` — will canary to one tenant. Monitor p99.

maria: Customer asked for immediate workaround while we root-cause. I'll propose rolling them to non-streaming fallback for the next 24h and issue credit if SLO breached. They'll accept if it reduces p99.

ben: Risk note — non-streaming will increase TTFB on their side (we bundle), but reduce chunking jitter. Suggested canary plan: 1) Apply coalesce_window_ms=50 for tenant for 1 hour. 2) If p99 improves by >200ms, promote and keep. 3) If not, switch to non-streaming fallback and notify customer. I'll open a quick rollout PR to infra.

ravi: Also check recent edge-proxy rollout log around 3949998000 — if the new proxy changed flush behavior we should correlate. I can pull proxy change diff (likely changed h2 windowing) and post in thread.

maria: Thanks — I'll run the tenant patch now and coordinate with Acme for repro window (15:30 UTC). I logged the customer support case and requested pcap if possible. Will update with metrics after the 1-hour canary. :white_check_mark:

ben: If you get the pcap, upload to S3 and ping me. We'll analyze HTTP/2 frames. Also add `x-request-debug: 1` header in their test to enable verbose routing logs.

maria: Filed follow-ups: support ticket updated, canary started, customer notified. (req-ACME-20260310-01 in case notes).
